scheme_name: Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation
description:
The Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation is a significant initiative under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY) launched on July 1, 2015.

This scheme aims to enhance irrigation efficiency and promote sustainable agricultural practices across India.

The primary objective of this initiative is to provide farmers with a reliable source of water for irrigation through the construction of water storage tanks.

These tanks are designed to facilitate drip irrigation systems which are known for their water conservation capabilities.

The government has set a target to construct approximately 1.5 million water storage tanks by the year 2025.

The scheme is particularly focused on regions that face water scarcity and have a high dependency on rainfall for agricultural activities.

The benefits of this scheme are manifold.

Farmers can expect an increase in crop yield due to the availability of a consistent water supply.

The construction of these tanks can reduce the dependency on groundwater, which is crucial given the alarming rates of groundwater depletion in many states.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme can cover up to 50% of the total cost of constructing a water storage tank.

For small and marginal farmers, the government offers a higher subsidy of up to 75% of the total cost.

The maximum financial assistance for the construction of a water storage tank is capped at INR 1 lakh.

Eligibility criteria for this scheme are clearly defined.

Farmers must possess a minimum of 0.5 hectares of agricultural land to qualify for the assistance.

The applicant must be a registered farmer under the relevant state agricultural department.

There are no specific educational qualifications required for eligibility.

The income ceiling for eligibility is set at INR 2 lakh per annum for small and marginal farmers.

The application process is straightforward and involves several steps.

Farmers must first approach their local agricultural department or the Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK).

They are required to fill out the application form which can be obtained from the respective office or downloaded from the official PMKSY website.

Along with the application form, farmers must submit proof of land ownership.

This can include land revenue records or any government-issued documents that establish ownership.

Farmers must also provide identity proof such as an Aadhar card or voter ID.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the local agricultural officer.

The officer will conduct a site visit to verify the details provided in the application.

If approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account.

The timeline for the entire application process can vary but typically takes around 30 to 45 days from submission to approval.

Disbursement of funds is usually done in a single installment once the application is approved.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

State governments also play a crucial role in the implementation of this scheme.

They are responsible for the ground-level execution and monitoring of the construction of water storage tanks.

Farmers can contact the local agricultural department for any queries related to the scheme.

The contact details of the local agricultural office can usually be found on the state government's agriculture department website.

In terms of statistics, the scheme has seen a significant uptake since its inception.

As of October 2023, over 500,000 water storage tanks have been constructed across various states.

This has directly benefited more than 1 million farmers by providing them with reliable irrigation facilities.

The scheme has also contributed to the conservation of water resources.

By promoting drip irrigation, it has helped reduce water usage in agriculture by approximately 30% compared to traditional irrigation methods.

The government has allocated a budget of INR 10,000 crore for the PMKSY scheme for the financial year 2023-2024.

This budget includes provisions for the construction of water storage tanks as well as other irrigation projects.

The scheme is expected to play a vital role in achieving the goal of doubling farmers' income by 2022.

The initiative aligns with the broader objectives of the National Water Policy which emphasizes the need for efficient water management in agriculture.

Farmers are encouraged to adopt modern irrigation techniques to maximize productivity while conserving water.

The success of the scheme is also attributed to the training and capacity-building programs organized by the government.

These programs educate farmers on the benefits of drip irrigation and the effective use of water storage tanks.

The government collaborates with various NGOs and agricultural universities to facilitate these training sessions.

Farmers are provided with hands-on training on the installation and maintenance of drip irrigation systems.

The scheme has also received positive feedback from various agricultural experts and organizations.

They emphasize that such initiatives are crucial for sustainable agriculture in the face of climate change.

The Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation is a vital step towards ensuring food security in India.

By providing farmers with the necessary resources and support, the government aims to create a more resilient agricultural sector.

The initiative is expected to contribute significantly to the overall economic development of rural areas.

As the scheme continues to evolve, the government remains committed to addressing the challenges faced by farmers.

This includes improving access to water resources and promoting sustainable agricultural practices.

The Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation is a testament to the government's dedication to enhancing the livelihoods of farmers across the nation.
